description: A force restart is the primary first-line recovery procedure for an Apple device that is frozen, exhibiting an unresponsive touchscreen, stuck on a black screen, or caught in a boot loop. Unlike a factory reset, a force restart does not erase data or settings from the device storage.
faqs:
Q: Does a force restart delete photos or files? A: No, a force restart only cuts power to RAM and forces reboot; it will not delete any stored user data.
Q: What should I do if the screen is still black after a force restart? A: Connect the device to an official Apple charger for at least 30 minutes, then attempt the force restart again while connected.
policy_terms: If force restart repeatedly fails or the device is stuck in a boot loop displaying the Apple logo, connect to a computer to enter Recovery Mode or schedule a Genius Bar appointment.

specs: Moisture Detection Alert: Liquid Detected in USB-C / Lightning Connector alert appears when pins detect conductivity. Actions TO TAKE: (1) Tap device gently against hand with connector facing down to remove excess liquid. (2) Leave device in dry area with airflow for at least 30 minutes up to 24 hours. Actions TO NEVER TAKE: Never put phone in raw rice (small rice particles scratch glass and damage ports); never insert cotton swabs or paper towels; never use hair dryers or compressed air.
description: Official Apple first-aid procedure when a device comes in contact with liquid or shows the Liquid Detected in Connector warning. Raw rice is explicitly warned against as starchy dust forms a corrosive paste inside the charging port and voids service eligibility.
faqs:
Q: Can I put my wet iPhone in rice? A: NO. Apple strictly warns never to put your iPhone in rice because tiny starch particles enter the connector and cause permanent damage.
Q: Can I charge my phone if the liquid alert appears? A: Do not charge via cable until the port is completely dry (usually 2 to 24 hours). If an emergency occurs, Qi/MagSafe wireless charging can be used if the back glass is dry.
Q: What should I do if the phone was dropped in saltwater? A: Rinse the affected exterior area gently with fresh tap water to remove corrosive salt, wipe dry with a lint-free cloth, and let dry thoroughly.
policy_terms: Using heat guns or hair dryers can permanently warp seals, damage screens, and void warranty.
